title: Round-by-round insertion sort process
summary: Each round inserts the immediately adjacent element on the right into the sorted prefix, expanding the prefix by one element.
context: The initial array is nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2], indexed from 0 to 5. A single-element range containing only the first element 4 is trivially sorted, so the initial "Sorted region" is [0, 0].
Each round selects the element immediately to the right of the sorted prefix as base, shifts elements greater than base to the right, and writes base into the vacated position.
description: The sorted prefix only guarantees relative order among its current elements; when smaller elements are inserted in later rounds, elements inside it may still shift right.

In the third round, when inserting the second 1, shifting stops as soon as it meets the equal first 1, preserving their original relative order. In the fourth round, 5 needs no movement while the sorted prefix still expands; the fifth round inserts 2 to complete the sort.

frames.title: Round-by-round insertion sort process
frames.explanation: After five rounds, the sorted prefix covers the entire array, and the two 1s retain their original order.

prose.title: Round-by-round insertion sort process
prose.summary: The six states correspond to the initial state followed by the states after rounds 1 through 5; each animation step number is 1 greater than the number of completed rounds.

steps.title: Start from a single-element prefix
steps.explanation: Initially, the first element 4 at index 0 forms the sorted prefix [0, 0] by itself; the next round will select 1 at index 1 as the base element to insert into the prefix.
steps.key_state: Initial state: nums = [4, 1, 3, 1, 5, 2], sorted prefix [0, 0]. Next base element: 1 at index 1.
steps.announcement: Starting from a sorted prefix containing only 4.

steps.title: Insert 1 before 4
steps.explanation: Round 1 selects 1 at index 1, shifts the larger element 4 right to index 1, and writes 1 to index 0, expanding the sorted prefix to [0, 1]. The next base element is 3 at index 2.
steps.key_state: After round 1: nums = [1, 4, 3, 1, 5, 2], sorted prefix [0, 1]. Next base element: 3 at index 2.

steps.title: Insert 3 between 1 and 4
steps.explanation: Round 2 selects 3 at index 2, shifts only 4 (greater than 3 in the prefix) right to index 2, and inserts 3 at index 1 (between 1 and 4), expanding the sorted prefix to [0, 2]. The next base element is 1 at index 3.
steps.key_state: After round 2: nums = [1, 3, 4, 1, 5, 2], sorted prefix [0, 2]. Next base element: 1 at index 3.

steps.title: Insert the second 1 after the first 1
steps.explanation: Round 3 selects the second 1 at index 3 and shifts 4 and 3 (both greater than 1 in the prefix) to the right in turn; upon reaching the equal first 1 at index 0, shifting stops immediately and the second 1 is inserted right after it at index 1, preserving the stable order of equal elements. The next base element is 5 at index 4. The sorted prefix is now [0, 3].
steps.key_state: After round 3: nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2], sorted prefix [0, 3]. Next base element: 5 at index 4. The two 1s keep their original order.
steps.announcement: Round 3 complete: inserted the second 1 after the first 1, preserving their original order.

steps.title: Include 5 in the sorted prefix
steps.explanation: Round 4 selects 5 at index 4; because 5 is greater than the largest element 4 in the sorted prefix [1, 1, 3, 4], no elements need to shift right and 5 joins the prefix in place, expanding the sorted prefix to [0, 4]. The next base element is 2 at index 5.
steps.key_state: After round 4: nums = [1, 1, 3, 4, 5, 2], sorted prefix [0, 4]. Next base element: 2 at index 5. No elements moved in this round, and 5 joined the prefix.
steps.announcement: Round 4 complete: 5 needed no movement, and the sorted prefix expanded.

steps.title: Insert 2 after the two 1s
steps.explanation: Round 5 selects 2 at the final index 5, shifts 5, 4, and 3 (all greater than 2 in the prefix) one position to the right in turn, and inserts 2 at index 2 after the two 1s; the sorted prefix now covers [0, 5], completing the sort.
steps.key_state: After round 5: nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], sorted prefix [0, 5]. Sorting complete.
steps.announcement: Round 5 complete: inserted 2 after the two 1s; sorting complete.
